questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always been fascinated by the French language, culture etc. This interest was sparked many years ago on family holidays, and when the opportunity of travelling to and studying in France was presented to me via the general information from the University of Copenhagen, I couldn't resist the temptation. The crucial aspects of choosing France – and not an English speaking country like many of my fellow students do – was the language. I simply wanted to enhance my French skills as well as trying to understand the Parisian lifestyle and French culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. But to many students it was very confusing to receive a bunch of information only in French. It did not seem very pedagogical and helpful. Also, to not receive the information need directly via email was frustrating. All information was provided through the University's website, and to navigate on this was not easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any direct and personal assistance but only general information. I quickly teamed up with other students in order to be able to find out what to do when and how.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was faily easy. I used a housing agency in order to find a reasonably situtated and well-equipped apartment.
I used
Lodgis.com
and would recommend it to everyone.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It can be lonely. 
It can be extremely comfortable to not share personal spaces such as bathroom, livingroom and kitchen with others. It can be expensive!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was extremely difficult to get an overview of the different courses. Whenever I wanted a specific course, the schedule collided with other courses – and this was unbeknownst to students choosing the different courses since the schedule for "travaux dirigés" was not visible online. These timetables were only visible when you met with the course administrator in person (to says the least, this was a complete outdated system with many flaws...).

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
1. Find the interesting courses online.
2. Show up to the courses in person in the 2 week trial period.
3. Book a meeting with the course administrator.
4. Select the courses with the course administrator and become frustrated when the timetables for the courses do not add up because of the collided schedules.
5. Quickly choose a different course from the one you wanted in first place.
6. Receive a printout of your selected courses (this seemed to me very outdated since receiving emails is a far more superior system...)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Only the course administrator (her name was Marion Bonnefond).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fairly succesful. I wanted two courses I couldn't have because of the colliding timetables. This meant I followed two courses I didn't want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared! There is not much help to receive and the system of choosing the courses is not transparent. Be patient and relaxed and hope for the best. There isn't much else to do...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was high. The professors were very well-prepared. There really isn't much else to elaborate on here.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Not at all. 
In Paris everything is taught in an old school fashion. There is not group work (except for in one class), there is no specific curriculum (it is only the material the teacher provides that is the curriculum), and there is no self-study (this meaning attendance at classes was mandatory in order to follow the courses). 
To me it seemed as if the students were not free to arrange their lives for themselves – they were simply to attached to the classes etc. Also the classes were held at outrages hours compared to at UCPH (some classses began as early as 7:45 in the morning, whereas others ended as late as 22:00 in the evening).
Also the written exams I had were multiple choice which is not a type of exam provided at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Droit civil
Relations internationales
Philosophy of Law
European Law
History of the European Legal System

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
It depends on the student's interests and desires. 
I believe international understand is important, and therefore courses in European Law and International Relations are important. These courses broaden the scope of understanding which in the future will be crucial.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected costs during my stay.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Books were way less expensive than I thought, simply because buying books wasn't required to follow the courses.
Food and general living costs are expensive in Paris, but not more expensive than I anticipated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All different kinds of sports, social soirées, job fairs etc. I found the university to always be full of life an activity.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sports! 
When you are new to a university getting to know other students is crucial. It can sometimes be difficult to befriend others in class, especially if there's a language barrier. But when playing sports it's way easier to talk to other students and to get to know them in a more comfortable atmosphere.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: During holidays and weekends it is really easy to take the TGV (high speed train) to other cultural sites or citys). I visited Bordeaux, Toulouse, Biarrtiz, Marseille, Geneva, Milan, Joyeuse as well as Giverny. France is a big country with many beautiful and interesting places, so the possibilities are endless.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was neither easy nor difficult. I have been to Paris many times before and knew the city quite well. The language barrier was probably the most difficult part, but just like anything else you quickly adapt.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to all the social acitivities available. Get to know your neighbourhood – once you know the owner of the local café just a little bit, it seems way more welcoming to sit down for a cup of coffee during weekends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The French have no logic and love bureaucracy. Everything is done in a much more complicated manner than necessary. Nothing too extreme, but very frustrating and challenging when trying to adapt to new surroundings.
There are plenty of cultural differences, and most of them are subtle.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the importance of cultural heritage and the architecture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be prepared and begin your application for exchange more than one semester before actually going abroad. There are many deadlines, forms, grants to be applied for etc. 
2. Be well aware of what your reasons are for going on exhange. Is it to enhance your resumé or is it because you actually have specific reasons for going to the desired place. I believe most people enjoy their semester abroad, but don't go if you feel a certain academic pressure – go because you want to. 
3. If you wish to study French law you need to speak French on a proper level. There is no mercy from professors or other students – so be prepared to be in classes, where it's everyone to himself.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have a girlfriend, very close family connections or friends that are close to you, be prepared for a very challenging experience. It is rewarding to go abroad but also difficult to keep the ties to the before mentioned people close and warm.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cultural understanding as well as my enhancement in French have been the two most rewarding parts of my exchange experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To miss friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
